sources.title: Uber Vehicle Marketplace
key_points: Uber says drivers can rent or buy a car for rideshare through vehicle partners.
Supports the core premise that Uber accepts rental-based entry.

sources.title: Uber Driver Requirements
key_points: Minimum age, driving experience, eligible 4-door vehicle, required documents, screening.
Uber also points drivers to rent or lease options.

sources.title: The Rideshare Guy — HyreCar Review 2026
key_points: Example pricing: 2020 Toyota Corolla in Los Angeles at about $375/week all-in.
Useful for rental economics, insurance framing, and practical renter workflow.
Also states HyreCar had shut down by 2026; used as market signal, not sole authority.

sources.title: Drive Whip — The Shutdown of HyreCar and Getaround
key_points: Used only as directional signal that peer-to-peer rideshare rental infrastructure has tightened.
Not treated as an authoritative source for policy or legal guidance.

sources.title: last30days raw export
key_points: Community evidence included examples of peer fleet pricing around $350/week.
Captured Reddit/social sentiment that many drivers feel Uber margins are tight.
Included anecdotal creator claims about scaling fleet-style rideshare rentals.

notes: Official Uber pages were treated as the highest-confidence sources for requirements and platform-sanctioned rental entry.
Profitability tables in summary.md are modeled scenario analyses built from researched rent points plus explicit operating assumptions.
Third-party shutdown commentary around HyreCar/Getaround was treated as contextual market signal only.
